title: Conic Sections: Parabolas, Ellipses and Hyperbolas
seo_title: Conic Sections Worksheet: Parabolas, Ellipses, Hyperbolas | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given the foci, using the fact that the sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on conic sections: parabolas, ellipses and hyperbolas with foci, vertices, directrix and asymptotes, identifying conics and applications. 100 questions.
key_big: Ellipse: c² = a² − b². Hyperbola: c² = a² + b².
key_sub: Parabola: the focus is p units from the vertex.
body_html:
How it works

  • Parabola (x − h)² = 4p(y − k): vertex (h, k), focus p units from the vertex, directrix p units on the other side.
  • Ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 (a > b): vertices at ±a, foci at ±c with c² = a² − b². The larger denominator shows the major axis.
  • Hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1: vertices at ±a, foci at ±c with c² = a² + b², asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x.
  • From Ax² + Cy² + …: A = C circle; same sign ellipse; opposite signs hyperbola; one squared term parabola.
Example

Find the foci of x²25 + y²9 = 1.

a² = 25 under x: horizontal

c² = 25 − 9 = 16, c = 4

Answer: (4, 0) and (−4, 0)

Example

Find the focus and directrix of x² = 8y.

4p = 8, p = 2

Opens up

Answer: focus (0, 2), directrix y = −2

Common mistakes

  • Using c² = a² + b² for an ellipse. That is for hyperbolas.
  • Using 4p as the distance to the focus. The distance is p.
  • Choosing the major axis from the first term instead of the larger denominator.
  • Flipping the signs of h and k: (x − 3) means h = 3.

faq.q: How do you find the foci of an ellipse?
faq.a: Use c² = a² − b², where a² is the larger denominator. The foci are c units from the center along the major axis.

faq.q: How do you find the foci of a hyperbola?
faq.a: Use c² = a² + b². The foci are c units from the center, on the same axis as the vertices.

faq.q: How do you find the focus of a parabola?
faq.a: Write it as (x − h)² = 4p(y − k) or (y − k)² = 4p(x − h). The focus is p units from the vertex, inside the curve.

faq.q: How can you tell which conic an equation is?
faq.a: Look at the squared terms: equal coefficients give a circle, same signs an ellipse, opposite signs a hyperbola, and only one squared term a parabola.
